key_insight: Positional disorder in realistic resonant dipole-dipole interacting networks can strongly localize excitations, even though the coupling is partly long-ranged and dissipative.
engineering_relevance: These localized quantum modes could help design more robust light-harvesting, excitonic, and quantum-sensing devices by controlling transport and storage of excitation energy.
method: Model spin/atom networks with realistic resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI).
Introduce positional disorder and analyze coherent plus dissipative coupling effects.
Compare excitation dynamics across geometries and wavelengths to identify localization behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a wavelength-induced transition from extended to localized excitation dynamics, with strong spatial localization emerging under disorder.
watch_item: Because the interaction is both radiative and dissipative, practical implementations must manage losses and geometry-dependent effects that may complicate device scaling.
paper_title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
